newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-UEFA ATTEMPTS TO UNRAVEL BOSNIA PROBLEM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA ATTEMPTS TO UNRAVEL BOSNIA PROBLEM.

text.p: Bosnian teams will not be allowed to compete in European competitions until the rival factions there agree which clubs represent the country, UEFA president Lennart Johansson said on Thursday.

There are currently three bodies in Bosnia -- the Muslim League, the Croatian League and the Serb League -- each organising their own league and cup championships. All three are affiliated to the Bosnia-Herzegovina Football Federation, which is recognised by FIFA.

But UEFA is not prepared to admit three teams from each of the leagues into Europe's three cup competitions -- the European Cup, the Cup Winners' Cup and the UEFA Cup. They want the leagues to agree on one representative for each competition.

So far no solution to the problem has been found and UEFA have now called for an urgent meeting between the leagues, the Bosnian football federation and FIFA to resolve the matter before the end of this season.

Johansson said on Thursday: "We are not prepared to deal with three football associations from one country. We will only deal with one entity. We cannot have three Bosnian champion teams in the European Cup for example. It cannot happen."
A UEFA source said one possible solution would a series of play-offs to establish what would effectively be a single Bosnian champion or cup winning team.
Soccer is returning to some degree of normality in Bosnia.

FIFA, world soccer's ruling body, recently agreed home World Cup matches can be played in the refurbished Kosevo Stadium in Sarajevo after earlier insisting Bosnia's home matches should be played on neutral territory.
After playing their opening World Cup qualifier against Croatia in Italy last October, Bosnia's first World Cup match scheduled for Sarajevo is against Greece on April 2.
As a result of FIFA's ruling for the national team, UEFA agreed on Thursday that the Bosnian Under-21 team, which comes under its jurisdiction, could also play its matches at home.
